title: C# 15 Unpacked: Practical Use Cases for Unions with Real Examples
why_read: A practical, example-driven tutorial on using C# discriminated unions for real problems like input validation and state machines, useful for .NET developers adopting this upcoming language feature.
analysis: This is the third part of a series explaining C# 15's new union types, moving from theory to concrete use cases like API result modeling, command handling, and state machines. It's a solid practical reference for .NET developers wanting to understand idiomatic patterns for a feature new to the language, even though algebraic/discriminated unions are old news in languages like Rust or F#. The content is instructional rather than novel research, so its value is mainly to C# developers specifically rather than a broader technical audience. It includes a companion GitHub repo for hands-on experimentation.
